stories.story: In the community music room, Nia wanted a duet for the picnic, with a drumbeat and an answering rhythm. She borrowed the little drum from the shelf; Dalia watched its red ribbon sway against Nia's wrist. Nia asked Mateo whether he would join her for a picnic duet, and waited for his answer. Mateo said he liked playing but did not want everyone watching him, holding his folder against his chest. Nia nodded and tried a quieter pattern on her drum, without asking him to change his mind. On Friday, she listed herself alone for a drum solo on the signup sheet, though she had imagined another name beside hers. She reshaped the pauses in her solo into a path of small beats, and found that the drum could answer itself. On Saturday, she performed her solo for the people gathered at the picnic, and let the last soft beat ring before the applause began. When the audience had gone, she kept her drum close and waited as the room settled, leaving room for an answer that might never come. She left the idea of playing together open for another time, glad that her solo had found its own shape. She put the borrowed drum back on the shelf, its red ribbon brushing the wooden edge. On the shelf, the ribbon rested between the two quiet drums, and Nia's solo still seemed to leave a little space for another day.

Among the mixed sounds of the music room, Nia wanted a duet for the picnic, with a drumbeat and an answering rhythm. She borrowed the little drum from the shelf; Dalia watched its red ribbon sway against Nia's wrist. She asked Mateo whether he would join her for a picnic duet, leaving a pause for him to decide. Mateo said he liked playing but did not want everyone watching him, with his eyes on the crowded room. Nia nodded and tried a quieter pattern on her drum, leaving space where another rhythm might have entered. On Friday, she wrote her own name and a drum solo on the signup sheet, rather than choosing for Mateo. She practiced the solo slowly on the rug, trying different volumes until the silence between beats felt like part of the song. On Saturday, she performed her solo for the people gathered at the picnic, filling the wide pauses with quieter beats until the room applauded. When the audience had gone, she kept her drum close and waited as the room settled, leaving room for an answer that might never come. Mateo said he was not ready to try a duet even in private; Nia nodded and gave him space. Nia put the borrowed drum back on the shelf, its red ribbon brushing the wooden edge. The two drums stood on the shelf with the red ribbon between them, while the last notes of Nia's solo faded in the quiet room.

Among the mixed sounds of the music room, Nia wanted a duet for the picnic, with one beat leaving room for another. She borrowed the little drum from the shelf; Dalia watched its red ribbon sway against Nia's wrist. She asked Mateo to play a duet with her at the picnic, and waited for his answer. Mateo said he liked playing but did not want everyone watching him, with his eyes on the crowded room. Nia nodded and glanced toward the spare instrument on the shelf, keeping her imagined answer to herself. On Friday, Nia wrote her own name and a drum solo on the signup sheet, though she had imagined another name beside hers. She worked through the solo beside the piano, trying different volumes until the silence between beats felt like part of the song. On Saturday, Nia played her drum solo before the picnic crowd, and let the last soft beat ring before the applause began. After the audience had gone, Nia invited Mateo to try a duet away from an audience, and told him he could say no. She left the idea of playing together open for another time, glad that her solo had found its own shape. Nia returned the borrowed drum to the shelf, and smoothed its red ribbon against the handle. On the shelf, the ribbon rested between the two quiet drums, while the last notes of Nia's solo faded in the quiet room.

Among the mixed sounds of the music room, Nia dreamed of a duet for the picnic, with a drumbeat and an answering rhythm. Nia took the little drum on loan from the shelf; Dalia watched its red ribbon sway against Nia's wrist. She asked Mateo to play a duet with her at the picnic, and waited for his answer. Mateo explained that he liked music but was not ready for an audience, holding his folder against his chest. Nia nodded and tried a quieter pattern on her drum, without asking him to change his mind. On Friday, she listed herself alone for a drum solo on the signup sheet, though she had imagined another name beside hers. She worked through the solo beside the piano, trying different volumes until the silence between beats felt like part of the song. On Saturday, she performed her solo for the people gathered at the picnic, filling the wide pauses with quieter beats until the room applauded. After the audience had gone, Nia asked Mateo whether he wanted to try the answer part privately, making it clear that the choice was his. Mateo said he would like to try the answer part with Nia on the rug, away from an audience. He picked up the spare drum from the shelf, testing its weight in his hands. He tapped the answer part on his drum and Nia answered on hers, with no name on a program and no audience to watch. He returned the second drum to the shelf, where its last vibration faded. Nia put the borrowed drum back on the shelf, its red ribbon brushing the wooden edge. On the shelf, the red ribbon hung between the two drums, while the last sound of their duet faded into the quiet room.
